---
title: "Equivalent reporting-loss scales"
subtitle: "5.2 · after Kline, Rose and Walters (2024), Section II"
description: "Affine equivalence of KRW's loss and postrank's risk over the six-site report family."
---

Scoring all 4,683 six-site reports by KRW's loss at λ and by postrank's risk at τ = λ/(1 + λ) relates both objectives by an increasing affine transformation.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **λ 1, flat line** gives slope 0; the full order has DR .0480 and expected correct minus wrong per pair .904 (Condorcet ranks).
- **λ .25** gives slope 3; both objectives choose 1/2/3/3/4/5 with postrank risk .0372.
- **τ .25, whole grid** checks 49 values of τ; both objectives return the same best-report set at 49 of 49 values.
- **λ .08** gives τ .0741 and coarsens the optimum to 1/1/2/2/3/3.
- **τ .40** sets λ to 2/3 and restores full order 1/2/3/4/5/6.

<details>
<summary>Scope and archived-card notes</summary>

The identity holds for the same posterior probabilities, target orientation, units, and report family. For every report, postrank's risk equals τ plus the product of one minus τ and KRW's risk at the matching λ. The residual records numerical rounding in this identity, and a tolerance determines which computed risks count as equal. KRW chose the archived 97-firm card using their original probabilities; the fixed-card evaluation in Data uses the released postrank probabilities, so it cannot establish that the card minimizes risk under those probabilities.

</details>
